newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh banks may flee to Russian T-bill market.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh banks may flee to Russian T-bill market.

text.p: Kazakh banks, worried by steeply falling yields on Treasury bills, may start investing in Russian securities rather than switch to long-term loans to local industry, dealers said on Friday.
"We do not like these low yields. Many banks will switch their investment to Russia's securities market," a dealer from Alfa Bank Kazakhstan said.
"As for foreign investors, they are happy about any yield."

The yield on Kazakh three-month MKM discount Treasury bills fell to 12.29 percent annual on Tuesday from 14.59 percent at the last auction on May 20. Six-month T-bills yielded 16.24 percent annual on Monday, compared to 19.90 percent on May 12.

The National Bank and the government have said that sharply falling yields reflected low inflation, which could fall this year below the official target of 17 percent, and stressed that operations with Kazakh T-bills were still profitable.
But many dealers disagree.
"Yields are too low, and many banks cannot cover interest rates on their deposit accounts in tenge by investing in T-bills," said Bank TuranAlem trader Nurlan Mukhametzhanov.
He said that many banks were interested in investing in foreign securities, "because in Kazakhstan there is no other instrument like T-bills".

"I simply cannot imagine who might invest in our government securities with such low yields. Most probably, foreigners -- the tenge is stable at around 75 per dollar, and even a yield of 10 percent annual is acceptable for them," Mukhametzhanov said.
He also said that banks might seek other securities markets.

"With their finances the banks will just go to other markets. Russian government securities are attractive because of large volumes of issues. There might also be good demand for Russian municipal paper because foreigners are allowed to buy them," Mukhametzhanov said.
"Almost all the banks... are determined to invest on the Russian market because low yields on Kazakh papers satisfy no one," said Kazkommertsbank dealer Denis Fedosenko.
The average yield on the Russian T-bill market on Friday was 23.6 percent.
Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin said earlier this week that low yields on Kazakh T-bills were likely to force local banks to turn to long-term loans to the rebounding economy.
But banks are sceptical about the premier's expectations.
"The government has worked out a draft law providing for tough punishment for overdue debts. But granting loans to the economy is still very problematic due to its bad shape," Mukhametzhanov said.

Next Monday the finance ministry will offer 450 million tenge of 12-month T-bills, which yielded 22.59 percent annual at the last auction on May 5. The government will offer 500 million of three-month paper on Tuesday.

Dealers said that yields on both papers next week would to a large extent depend on whether the National Bank announced a new auction of its notes issued to sterilise the money supply and support the national tenge currency.

"If the notes are issued, they could attract much money, and T-bill yields might be unchanged...But the National Bank has said earlier it might stop issuing notes this summer, and summer starts next week," Mukhametzhanov said.
--Almaty Newsroom, +7 3272 509410
